text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Routing SLO breach detected: router.p99 >= 2.3s in region=us-west-2, streaming stalls observed. Pager sent to #oncall (maya)
maya: I’m on it. seeing p95 ~ 620ms but p99 jumping to 2s+. Streams showing stalls around heavy multi-partition keys.
sam: grabbing routing tables + LB shard maps. running query: `select count(*) from requests where latency>2000 and region='us-west-2' group by route`
sam: raw looks noisy, but one logical shard group has 60% of the >2s tails. suspect misroute/weighting on new traffic steering policy rolled 10m ago.
dana: can you share the policy id? I’ll check rollout status and canary percentage.
sam: policy_id=route-steer-v17, rollout=75% in us-west-2, previous v16.
leo: omg that's the one we pushed for affinity improvements. I see hot-key reassignments in the telemetry.
maya: customer-impact: small fraction of requests (~0.8% overall) but impacting streaming customers with long tails and some reconnects. CS says two enterprise customers reported degraded streaming QoS. @customer-support please capture customer IDs.
customer-support: customers affected: acme-inc, finlytics. raised support tickets 21871,21872. Logged errors: connection resets and seek stalls.
ash (ops-bot): incident-bot pinned runbook: `routing-rollout-rollback`
maya: proposal: rollback route-steer-v17 to v16 in us-west-2 immediately to stop misassignment. Also immediate mitigation: temporarily throttle the heavy logical shard to reduce hot partitioning.
dana: I can rollback via control-plane, command: `redwood ctl rollout --policy route-steer-v17 --rollback-to route-steer-v16 --region us-west-2` — but need approval from oncall.
maya: approving. execute rollback and monitor p99.
ops-bot: executing rollback job j-89342 (initiated by dana)
ops-bot: rollback started...
sam: while rollback runs, I've prepared an emergency LB weight patch: `curl -XPOST https://lb.internal/api/weights -d '{"shard":"shard-07","weight":0.25}'` to deflate hot shard. Holding until rollback completes.
leo: PRD note: route-steer-v17 introduced per-key affinity with sticky weight rebalance; looks like a bug where keys with high fanout were pinned to fewer router replicas -> hot partitions -> queueing.
ops-bot: rollback complete (job j-89342). route-steer-v16 active in us-west-2.
maya: metrics: p99 dropped from 2.3s -> 380ms over next 90s. streaming stall count down 92%. customers reporting partial recovery.
customer-support: updated tickets 21871/21872 with mitigation notes and ETA for postmortem.
dana: follow-up actions: 1) block route-steer-v17 rollout until postmortem; 2) add synthetic prompts to exercise high-fanout keys in canary; 3) add alert to detect shard weight concentration (new metric: shard_top3_pct > 45%).
sam: I'll push a quick telemetry query to surface top-k shard concentration and make it visible on the oncall dashboard. query: `topk(3, sum by(shard)(requests)) / sum(requests)`
leo: logging patch: add trace id at router handoff point to make misroute analysis easier.
maya: oncall handoff: I'm staying until stabilization window ends (30m), then handoff to leo if everything stays green.
ops-bot: reminder: create postmortem draft in /incidents/postmortems/ - template linked: https://redwood.internal/templates/pm-routing.json
ash (incident-bot): Post-incident checklist: severity=P2, impact=streaming degradation for select customers, mitigation=rollback + weight patch, next steps=postmortem + rollout gating.
ash (incident-bot): tagging oncall rotation: @dana @leo for follow-ups.
leo: noted. will start root cause writeup and schedule follow-up sync with eng-runtime and eng-platform tomorrow.
maya: thanks team. final note: if anyone has a reproduction snippet for high-fanout key pattern please drop it here — we need one for the canary harness. :thumbsup:
